projects.title: Suspicious PowerShell Detection Lab
projects.summary: Practice detection from evidence, not from a copied rule.
projects.why: Practice detection from evidence, not from a copied rule.
projects.process: Generated events, inspected process trees and command lines, then replayed the activity.
projects.takeaway: Context matters more than one suspicious string.
projects.evidence:
$ labctl run powershell-detection
signal = powershell.exe
parent = winword.exe
host = lab-win-01
user = analyst
projects.body:
## Write-up

I built a small Windows lab to practice turning telemetry into a detection hypothesis before writing a rule.

### What I looked at
- Parent and child process relationships
- PowerShell command-line context
- Host and user context
- Replayed events to see what held up

### Notes
The important part was not the final rule. It was learning which pieces of evidence changed the confidence of the investigation.

projects.title: Web App Access-Control Review
projects.summary: Test one change at a time and document exactly what the server allows.
projects.why: Practice authorization testing by changing one thing at a time.
projects.process: Mapped endpoints, captured baseline requests, changed identifiers and roles, then compared responses and side effects.
projects.takeaway: The original request, changed input, and resulting behavior belong together in the write-up.
projects.evidence:
GET /api/invoices/1042
Authorization: Bearer <lab-token>

# Change only the resource id.
projects.body:
## Write-up

Mapped endpoints, captured baseline requests, changed identifiers and roles, then compared the server's behavior.

### Notes
Keep the original request, the one changed variable, and the response next to each other so the finding is easy to verify.

projects.title: Phishing Triage Exercise
projects.summary: Turn a vague suspicious-email report into a structured incident timeline.
projects.why: Practice moving from a first report to a defensible timeline.
projects.process: Reviewed headers and URLs, reconstructed the timeline, checked authentication activity, and listed containment steps.
projects.takeaway: Keep findings tied to evidence before jumping to a conclusion.
projects.evidence:
Indicators
- reply-to mismatch
- lookalike domain
- unexpected sign-in

Containment
- revoke sessions
- reset credentials
projects.body:
## Write-up

Worked from the initial report toward a concise timeline and containment checklist.

projects.title: PCAP Investigation: Beaconing Pattern
projects.summary: Reduce a noisy packet capture to a small, defensible hypothesis.
projects.why: Get more comfortable moving from noise to a defensible network hypothesis.
projects.process: Started with DNS and connection frequency, then checked timing, destinations, and protocol details.
projects.takeaway: Filtering is half the work. Writing down why each filter is useful keeps the investigation reproducible.
projects.body:
## Write-up

Started with broad traffic, filtered toward repeated patterns, then documented why each filter mattered.

projects.title: Python Asset Snapshot Tool
projects.summary: Make recurring checks consistent with small, predictable automation.
projects.why: Replace ad hoc host checks with a repeatable utility.
projects.process: Built a CLI with validation, explicit failures, and JSON output that can be diffed later.
projects.takeaway: Small security tools become more useful when their output is predictable and boring.
projects.body:
## Write-up

A small CLI for repeatable host checks with output designed to be compared later.
